explanation: Kalai's MO problem, literal version: for every monotone F and interval [s,t] with t/s > 1000 log n, some p ∈ [s,t] makes F optimal, i.e. I^p(F) ≤ 1000 log(1/p) · μ_p(F) log_p μ_p(F)/p. The μ_p, h(S), I^p and optimality definitions match the MO post. The Lean negates the universal statement, matching the docstring's report of Perles' counterexample to the version without μ_t(F) = 1/2, with a linked formal proof. The statement is faithful.
